chunks: Fadalah ibn 'Uthman narrated from Fudayl ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'Advise me.' He said, 'I advise you to have God-consciousness, be truthful in speech, fulfill the trusts, and be a good companion to those who accompany you. When it is before sunrise and before sunset, you should engage in supplication. Strive [in this] and do not hold back from asking anything from your Lord, and do not say, "This is something He will not give," but supplicate, for indeed Allah does what He wills.'
ai.seo_question: What are the key ethical virtues and recommended times for supplication according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) outlines a comprehensive spiritual protocol for Fadalah ibn Ubayd, emphasizing that sincerity in speech and trustworthiness are foundational to divine proximity. He specifically prescribes the times of *Duha* (late morning) and *Asr* (afternoon) for supplication, encouraging believers to adopt an attitude of confident expectation (*Yaqeen*) rather than hesitation, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the efficacy of prayer when coupled with persistent effort (*Ijtihad*).
